description: An Intelligent Microgravity Combustion Research Explorer
summary:
FlameLab AI is an interactive, AI-assisted research dashboard developed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research more accessible, understandable, and easier to compare.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity, creating unique safety challenges for astronauts and spacecraft during long-duration space missions. However, findings from combustion investigations are distributed across multiple research projects, making them difficult to explore collectively.

FlameLab AI addresses this challenge through a Research Explorer, a retrieval-based SI Research Assistant, side-by-side study comparisons, and visual research insights. Using Python, Streamlit, and TF-IDF-based text relevance matching, the application helps users discover relevant NASA combustion investigations and explore their research.

The current prototype features a curated catalogue of 12 NASA investigation summaries, with links to original sources. It is an exploratory research tool rather than a validated fire-risk prediction system.

By improving access to existing research, FlameLab AI aims to support better understanding of microgravity combustion and contribute to safer future human space exploration.
details:
FlameLab AI

Exploring Microgravity Combustion Research Through an Intelligent Research Dashboard

The Problem

Understanding fire behaviour in microgravity is essential for protecting astronauts and spacecraft during long-duration space missions. However, NASA's combustion research is spread across multiple investigations, making it difficult to explore and compare findings efficiently.

My Solution

FlameLab AI is an interactive research dashboard designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, understand and compare.

The application provides:

  • Research Explorer: Search and explore a curated catalogue of NASA combustion investigations.
  • SI Research Assistant: Retrieve relevant research information in response to user queries.
  • Study Comparison: Compare different combustion investigations side by side.
  • Research Insights: Explore research themes and catalogue-level statistics.
  • Source Transparency: Access references and understand the methodology behind the dashboard.

Technology Used

The project is developed using Python and Streamlit. It uses text-processing and TF-IDF-based relevance matching to identify research records related to user queries.

Scientific Approach

FlameLab AI currently uses a curated catalogue of 12 NASA combustion investigation summaries. It is an exploratory research tool, not a validated fire-risk prediction system. Its current version does not analyse the complete raw experimental datasets.

Future Scope

Future development could integrate NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics datasets, experimental measurements and video observations. More advanced AI methods could then help identify patterns across investigations and support evidence-based fire-safety research for space exploration.

My Vision

To make valuable microgravity combustion research more accessible, interpretable and useful for understanding fire safety in future human space missions.
